CVE-2022-26505.title: A DNS rebinding issue in ReadyMedia (formerly MiniDLNA) before 1. ...
CVE-2022-26505.description: A DNS rebinding issue in ReadyMedia (formerly MiniDLNA) before 1.3.1 allows a remote web server to exfiltrate media files.

CVE-2023-33476.title: ReadyMedia (MiniDLNA) versions from 1.1.15 up to 1.3.2 is vulnera ...
CVE-2023-33476.description: ReadyMedia (MiniDLNA) versions from 1.1.15 up to 1.3.2 is vulnerable to Buffer Overflow. The vulnerability is caused by incorrect validation logic when handling HTTP requests using chunked transport encoding. This results in other code later using attacker-controlled chunk values that exceed the length of the allocated buffer, resulting in out-of-bounds read/write.

CVE-2026-29508.title: ReadyMedia (formerly MiniDLNA) versions 1.3.0 through 1.3.3 conta ...
CVE-2026-29508.description: ReadyMedia (formerly MiniDLNA) versions 1.3.0 through 1.3.3 contain a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows remote attackers to corrupt stack memory by crafting a malicious DFF audio file with an oversized PROP chunk size value that is used unvalidated to allocate a variable-length stack array and read file data into it. Attackers can place a crafted DFF file in a directory monitored by ReadyMedia to trigger automatic parsing via inotify, achieving remote code execution on unprotected builds or denial of service on hardened builds with stack protections.
